We got list of templates. Need to pick one that breaks sulfonamide and amide? The first template seems to break sulfonamide? It shows retro_smarts: [O]=S(=O)-...-NH-... to ... maybe breaks S-N? Actually retro_smarts_template: [O;D1;H0:1]=[#16:2](=[O;D1;H0:3])(-[c:4])-[NH;D2;+0:5]-[c;H0;D3;+0:9]...>>... It seems to break the sulfonamide bond? The product side is same? Hard.

But we can use this template to generate precursors. Let's apply template to target molecule. Need template_id? The result includes reaction_id and template_hash but not template_id. Might need to use get_template with ID? The tool expects template_id string. The search result may not give ID. Might be reaction_id? Could use reaction_id as template_id? Not sure.

Alternative: Use apply_template directly with a known template ID from literature? Might be easier to propose a plausible route manually without using tools, but need to ensure leaves are commercially available. We can assume simple building blocks: 4-methyl aniline (p-toluidine) for the left phenyl with methyl, 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride for sulfonyl part, and trans-cinnamoyl aniline (maybe trans-4-aminocinnamic acid) etc.

But need to ensure commercial availability and price under $9999. Likely yes.

We can propose three-step synthesis:

Step1: Form sulfonamide: React p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) with 4-(2-((E)-cinnamoyl)anilino)benzenesulfonyl chloride? Actually target has sulfonyl attached to second phenyl which also has a cinnamoyl amide attached to an aniline. So maybe first make sulfonyl chloride from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride then substitute with p-toluidine.

But we need route: Starting materials: p-toluidine (commercial), 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial), trans-cinnamic acid (commercial), aniline (commercial). Then steps:

1) Couple aniline with trans-cinnamic acid via amide formation (using coupling reagent) to give N-phenylcinnamamide (cinnamoyl aniline). This is the fragment attached to second phenyl via amide? Actually target has .../C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So the amide attaches to phenyl ring at position para to sulfonamide? The amide carbonyl attached to phenyl ring (c2) and then attached to aniline (c3). So we need to attach amide to phenyl ring (c2) via carbonyl linking to aniline.

Thus we could first make 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride? Wait.

Better: Disconnection: Break amide bond between carbonyl and aniline (Nc3...). So precursor A: 4-(sulfonamido)phenylacrylic acid (i.e., phenyl with sulfonamide and attached to C=C-COOH). Precursor B: aniline.

Then step2: Form amide between acid and aniline using coupling.

Step1: Form sulfonamide between p-toluidine and 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride to give p-tolyl-sulfonamide attached to phenyl ring (with bromide maybe). Then do Suzuki coupling to attach the cinnamoyl side chain? Actually the phenyl ring also has a vinyl carbonyl side chain (C=C-CO-). Could be introduced via Heck reaction of bromophenyl sulfonamide with acrylamide? Actually we need C=C-CO-NH-PhNH2 attached.

Simplify: Use commercially available 4-(methyl)phenylsulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) reacts with 4-aminophenyl (the second phenyl) to give sulfonamide linking two phenyls? Wait p-toluenesulfonyl chloride has sulfonyl attached to methyl phenyl; reacting with aniline gives p-toluenesulfonamide (p-CH3C6H4SO2NHPh). That matches left side: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O) ... )cc1 where left phenyl is methyl-substituted and attached via N to sulfonyl. So sulfonyl derived from p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (commercial). React with 4-aminophenyl that also bears the cinnamoyl amide substituent.

Thus we need precursor: 4-aminophenyl with side chain /C=C/C(=O)NH-PhNH2. That is 4-(cinnamoyl)aniline? Actually the side chain is attached to phenyl via the double bond: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-PhNH2. So the phenyl (c2) has a vinyl carbonyl attached to an aniline. So we need 4-(E)-cinnamoylaniline? Wait the phenyl c2 has substituent /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. So the phenyl attaches at the carbon of the double bond (the beta carbon). So the phenyl is attached to the alkene carbon (the one adjacent to carbonyl). So the fragment is trans-β-aryl acrylamide.

Thus we can start from 4-bromo-phenyl (or 4-iodo) to do Heck coupling with acrylamide (or protected). But we need final amide with aniline.

Simplify route: Step1: Synthesize trans-β-aryl acrylamide by Heck coupling of 4-iodoaniline (or 4-iodobenzene) with acrylamide? Actually need aniline attached to carbonyl after coupling. Could start from trans-cinnamic acid, convert to acid chloride, then amidate with aniline to give trans-cinnamamide (Ph-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph). Then perform bromination at para position of the phenyl (the one attached to carbonyl) to introduce sulfonyl? But we need sulfonamide attached to that phenyl at para position? Actually the phenyl attached to carbonyl (c3) is an aniline (has NH2) that is not further substituted. So the sulfonamide attaches to the other phenyl (c2) which is para-substituted with the vinyl amide.

Thus we can have two phenyl rings: Ring A (left) methyl phenyl with sulfonamide linking to Ring B (center). Ring B has para vinyl amide substituent linking to Ring C (aniline). So we can construct:

- Prepare Ring B sulfonyl chloride (4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride) maybe? Actually we need sulfonyl attached to Ring A via N, and Ring B is attached to sulfonyl as the sulfonyl aryl group. So sulfonyl chloride derived from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (or 4-iodo). React with p-toluidine to give sulfonamide linking Ring A and Ring B (with bromide on Ring B para position). Then perform Heck coupling of that bromophenyl sulfonamide with trans-cinnamoyl aniline (or with acrylamide then amidate). But the vinyl side chain attaches at para position of Ring B (where bromide is). So we can do Heck coupling of the bromophenyl sulfonamide with acrylamide (CH2=CH-CO-NH-Ph). That yields the desired C=C-CO-NH-Ph attached to Ring B. That gives final product.

Thus steps:

1) Sulfonamide formation: p-toluidine + 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride → sulfonamide intermediate (Ring A–SO2–NH–Ring B-Br). (commercial reagents)

2) Heck coupling: intermediate + trans-cinnamamide (or acrylamide with aniline) → product with vinyl amide attached (Ring B now has C=C-CO-NH-Ph). Use Pd catalyst.

But we need also the aniline attached to carbonyl; the acrylamide already contains aniline. So we need trans-cinnamamide (Ph-CH=CH-CO-NH2) then amidate with aniline? Actually trans-cinnamamide already has aniline? Wait cinnamamide is CH=CH-CO-NH2 (no phenyl on amide). We need CO-NH-PhNH2 (aniline attached). So we need N-phenylcinnamamide (Ph-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph). That's trans-N-phenylcinnamamide, which can be made by coupling trans-cinnamic acid with aniline (amide formation). So we can have that as reagent.

Thus step2: Heck coupling of bromophenyl sulfonamide with trans-N-phenylcinnamamide (which has a double bond). However Heck coupling typically works with alkenes like acrylates, not amides? Might still work.

Alternatively, we could first do Heck coupling with acrylate then amidate. Simpler: Use trans-cinnamic acid (commercial) to form acid chloride then amidate with aniline to give N-phenylcinnamamide (commercial maybe). Could be purchased directly.

Thus final route 2 steps: (1) sulfonamide formation, (2) Heck coupling.

We need to ensure leaves are commercially available: p-toluidine, 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride, trans-N-phenylcinnamamide (maybe not commercial). Could use trans-cinnamic acid and aniline as separate leaves, then need extra step for amide formation (makes 3 steps). That's within limit.

Thus three-step route:

Step1: Form N-phenylcinnamamide: trans-cinnamic acid + aniline → amide (using coupling reagent). Leaves: trans-cinnamic acid, aniline (both commercial).

Step2: Form sulfonamide: p-toluidine + 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride → sulfonamide intermediate. Leaves: p-toluidine, 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial).

Step3: Heck coupling: sulfonamide intermediate (with bromophenyl) + N-phenylcinnamamide (alkene) → target molecule.

Thus total leaves: p-toluidine, 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride, trans-cinnamic acid, aniline. All commercial, price likely under $10k.

Now need to produce JSON route. Need template IDs for each reaction. We need to find templates for sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + amine) and amide formation (acid + amine) and Heck coupling (aryl bromide + alkene). Use search to find templates.

Search for sulfonamide formation: functional_groups_formed=["sulfonamides"], functional_groups_broken maybe none.
